## Task
Optimize a continuous-flow Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of an aryl bromide with an arylboronic acid (phosphine-ligated Pd catalyst, aqueous base / organic co-solvent). Each experiment sets six process conditions -- temperature (°C), back-pressure (bar), Pd loading (mol%), residence time (min), pH of the aqueous phase, and the water volume fraction of the solvent -- and reports the isolated yield of the biaryl product (%) and a relative cost index for the run. Goal: maximize the yield.

## Inputs
| parameter | type | domain | scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `temperature` | real | [0, 150] | linear |
| `pressure` | real | [1, 10] | linear |
| `catalyst_loading` | real | [0.1, 10] | log |
| `residence_time` | real | [1, 180] | log |
| `pH` | real | [6, 13] | linear |
| `water_fraction` | real | [0, 1] | linear |

## Outputs
- `yield`: objective; maximize (higher is better). Isolated yield of the biaryl product in %.
- `cost`: reported for information; not optimized. Relative cost index of the run (Pd, heating time, pressurization); lower is cheaper.

## Noise
Observations are noiseless: repeated evaluations of the same input return the same value.

Practitioner experience with aqueous-organic Suzuki-Miyaura couplings of this kind: the ligated Pd catalyst usually performs best at moderately elevated temperature, roughly 70-100 °C; near room temperature the reaction is sluggish and the catalyst tends to die before conversion is complete, while above about 110 °C the phosphine ligand degrades quickly (palladium black) and the biaryl product starts to decompose during long holds. The aqueous phase must be clearly basic to activate the boronic acid (pH of roughly 10-12 is typical), but strongly caustic conditions accelerate protodeboronation. Biphasic mixtures with a minority water phase (about 20-40 % water) generally outperform both anhydrous and water-rich media. Pd loadings of about 0.5-3 mol% are standard: more catalyst brings diminishing returns, and very high loadings promote aggregation and homocoupling. At these temperatures residence times of roughly 20-90 minutes are normally sufficient, and a modest back-pressure of a few bar mainly serves to keep the solvent from boiling.
